categories.name: Mammals
categories.tagline: Warm-blooded, furry, and fed on mother's milk.
categories.blurb: Mammals have hair or fur and are warm-blooded. Most give birth to live young and feed them milk. Examples: humans, lions, cats, elephants.
categories.intro: From tiny bats to the giant whales of the open ocean, mammals live on every continent and in every sea. What they share: fur or hair, warm blood, and milk for their young.
categories.didyouknow: The platypus and the echidna are mammals that lay eggs.

categories.name: Birds
categories.tagline: Feathers, wings, and songs from every sky.
categories.blurb: Birds have feathers, wings and beaks, and no teeth. All birds lay eggs, and most can fly. Examples: sparrow, pigeon, eagle, penguin.
categories.intro: There are around 10,000 species of birds, from hummingbirds that weigh less than a coin to eagles that hunt from high above. Every one of them has feathers and lays eggs.
categories.didyouknow: Owls cannot move their eyes, so they turn their heads, up to about 270 degrees.

categories.name: Fish
categories.tagline: Gills, fins, and the whole blue planet.
categories.blurb: Fish are aquatic vertebrates, from bony fish to sharks and rays. They live in nearly every kind of water, from rivers and lakes to the deep sea.
categories.intro: Fish breathe underwater with gills and swim with fins. They live in rivers, lakes, coral reefs and the deep sea, and they come in more shapes and sizes than any other group of vertebrates.
categories.didyouknow: Some deep-sea fish make their own light. This is called bioluminescence.

categories.name: Insects
categories.tagline: Six legs, three body parts, endless variety.
categories.blurb: Insects have six legs and a body in three parts: head, thorax and abdomen. Many have wings, and they are the largest group of animals. Examples: bee, butterfly, ant.
categories.intro: Insects are small animals with six legs and three main body parts: the head, the thorax (middle) and the abdomen (end). They live almost everywhere, pollinate flowers, and recycle dead plants and animals.
categories.didyouknow: There are more species of beetles than of any other group of animals.

categories.name: Arachnids
categories.blurb: Arachnids are eight-legged arthropods with two body sections and no antennae. Spiders, scorpions, mites and ticks belong here. Most feed on insects.
categories.intro: They crawl, they spin, they hunt. Arachnids are not just spiders: scorpions, mites and ticks are arachnids too. Most of them help nature by eating insects.
categories.didyouknow: Arachnids differ from insects: arachnids have 8 legs and no wings.

categories.name: Mollusks
categories.tagline: Soft bodies, clever minds, shells for some.
categories.blurb: Mollusks have soft bodies, and some have a shell for protection. Some live in the sea, others on land. Examples: snail, octopus, clam.
categories.intro: Mollusks are soft-bodied animals. Many have a shell, and they live in oceans, rivers and on land. Most have a head, a soft body and a muscular foot to move.

categories.name: Reptiles
categories.blurb: Reptiles are cold-blooded animals covered in scales. Snakes, lizards, turtles and crocodiles all belong here, and most lay eggs.
categories.intro: Reptiles are covered in dry scales and rely on the sun to warm their bodies. Most lay eggs on land. Their family includes snakes, lizards, turtles, crocodiles and the rare tuatara.
categories.didyouknow: The tuatara of New Zealand is the last of a group that lived alongside the dinosaurs.

animals.name: Kangaroo
animals.alt: A kangaroo standing in dry grassland
animals.summary: Strong back legs and a sturdy tail make kangaroos built for hopping, grazing and getting away from danger.
animals.habitat: Grasslands, scrub and woodland of Australia
animals.fun: A kangaroo cannot walk backwards easily, and a newborn joey is only about the size of a jellybean.

animals.name: Platypus
animals.alt: A platypus resting on a muddy bank
animals.summary: A mammal that lays eggs. The male has a sharp spur on each back heel that delivers venom.
animals.habitat: Rivers and streams in eastern Australia and Tasmania
animals.diet: Worms, shrimps and insect larvae found on the riverbed
animals.fun: It hunts with its eyes closed, sensing the electricity of its prey with its bill.

animals.name: Lion
animals.alt: A lion lying on a rock
animals.summary: Lions are the only big cats that live in groups. A group, called a pride, can have up to about 30 lions depending on the food and water available.
animals.habitat: African savannas and grasslands
animals.diet: Meat (carnivore), mostly zebra, wildebeest and antelope
animals.fun: A lion's roar can be heard from about 8 kilometres away.

animals.name: Zebra
animals.alt: Two zebras standing together
animals.summary: The black-and-white stripes help zebras recognise each other, and they may also confuse biting flies and predators.
animals.habitat: Grasslands and open woodland of eastern and southern Africa
animals.fun: No two zebras have exactly the same stripe pattern.

animals.name: Giraffe
animals.alt: A giraffe's head and neck
animals.summary: Giraffes can sprint at about 55 km/h over short distances, or cruise at about 16 km/h over longer ones.
animals.habitat: Savannas and open woodland of Africa
animals.fun: A giraffe's tongue is about 45 cm long and dark purple, which protects it from the sun.

animals.name: Whale
animals.alt: An orca leaping out of the sea
animals.summary: Whales are social, air-breathing mammals. They give birth to live young and feed their babies with their own milk.
animals.habitat: Oceans all over the world
animals.diet: Fish, squid or tiny krill, depending on the species
animals.fun: Whales are mammals, not fish. They come to the surface to breathe through a blowhole.

animals.name: Bat
animals.alt: A bat in flight with its wings spread
animals.summary: Bats are the only mammals that can truly fly. Many use echolocation, calling out and listening to the echoes, to find their way at night.
animals.habitat: Caves, forests and cities on every continent except Antarctica
animals.diet: Insects, fruit or nectar, depending on the species
animals.fun: A single small bat can eat thousands of insects in one night.

animals.name: Bald eagle
animals.alt: A bald eagle soaring in front of mountains
animals.summary: A powerful bird of prey known for its strength and very sharp eyesight. It often snatches fish from the surface of the water.
animals.habitat: Near lakes, rivers and coasts in North America
animals.diet: Fish, plus small animals and carrion
animals.fun: Its nest can grow into the largest tree nest of any bird in North America.

animals.name: Falcon
animals.alt: A falcon with wings spread wide
animals.summary: A fast, powerful bird of prey known for its speed and hunting skill.
animals.habitat: Open country, cliffs and cities across most of the world
animals.fun: The peregrine falcon is the fastest animal on Earth, diving at over 300 km/h.

animals.name: Owl
animals.alt: A barred owl perched in a leafy tree
animals.summary: A mostly nocturnal bird known for seeing in the dark and for its deep "hoo" call.
animals.habitat: Forests, farmland and deserts on every continent except Antarctica
animals.fun: Owls fly almost silently because of the soft edges of their feathers.

animals.name: Lovebird
animals.alt: A green lovebird with a peach face among flowers
animals.summary: A small, colourful bird that sings and chirps. Lovebirds are named for the close bond between mates.
animals.habitat: Woodland and savanna in Africa; popular as pets worldwide
animals.fun: Lovebirds often sit in pairs and preen each other's feathers.

animals.name: Parrot
animals.alt: A red, yellow and blue macaw perched on a branch
animals.summary: A colourful, intelligent bird that can mimic human speech and other sounds.
animals.habitat: Tropical and subtropical forests
animals.fun: Many parrots can live for decades, and some for more than 60 years.

animals.name: Clownfish
animals.summary: Clownfish live safely among the stinging tentacles of sea anemones on coral reefs. This is the fish that inspired Nemo.
animals.habitat: Warm coral reefs of the Indian and Pacific oceans
animals.fun: All clownfish are born male, and the biggest one in a group can become female.

animals.name: Shark
animals.summary: Sharks are fish with skeletons of cartilage, not bone. Most sharks are not dangerous to people, and many are very important to ocean health.
animals.habitat: Oceans worldwide, from shallow coasts to the deep sea
animals.diet: Mostly fish and squid; whale sharks filter tiny plankton
animals.fun: Sharks have been around for more than 400 million years, longer than trees.

animals.name: Pufferfish
animals.summary: When threatened, a pufferfish gulps water and swells into a ball. Many are poisonous if eaten.
animals.habitat: Tropical and subtropical seas, and some rivers
animals.fun: Pufferfish have no scales and cannot swim fast, so their trick is to puff up.

animals.name: Goldfish
animals.summary: A hardy freshwater fish kept as a pet for centuries. Goldfish can live for a decade or more with good care.
animals.habitat: Freshwater ponds and aquariums
animals.fun: Goldfish can see colours, including some that humans cannot.

animals.name: Fly
animals.alt: A fly on a green leaf
animals.summary: A small insect with two wings that flies quickly. Flies often live near people and land on food and garbage.
animals.habitat: Almost everywhere people live
animals.fun: A fly can beat its wings about 200 times every second.

animals.name: Butterfly
animals.alt: A blue butterfly with open wings resting on gravel
animals.summary: A colourful insect with large wings. It goes through four life stages: egg, larva (caterpillar), pupa and adult.
animals.habitat: Gardens, meadows and forests on every continent except Antarctica
animals.diet: Nectar as adults; leaves as caterpillars
animals.fun: Butterflies taste with their feet.

animals.name: Bee
animals.alt: A honey bee collecting pollen from a yellow flower
animals.summary: A flying insect that collects nectar and makes honey. Bees also pollinate flowers and plants.
animals.habitat: Meadows, gardens and orchards; hives in hollow trees or boxes
animals.fun: A honey bee visits hundreds of flowers on a single trip.

animals.name: Beetle
animals.alt: A red ladybird on a mushroom
animals.summary: A hard-bodied insect with two pairs of wings. Some beetles, like the ladybird, are helpful gardeners, while others damage crops.
animals.habitat: Nearly every land and freshwater habitat
animals.diet: Plants, other insects or decaying matter
animals.fun: Roughly one in every four known animal species is a beetle.

animals.name: Ant
animals.alt: A red ant on a branch
animals.summary: A small insect that lives in colonies. Ants are strong for their size and work together in groups.
animals.habitat: Soil, wood and leaf litter on every continent except Antarctica
animals.diet: Seeds, other insects and sweet liquids
animals.fun: An ant can carry many times its own body weight.

animals.name: Locust
animals.alt: A grasshopper clinging to a grass stem
animals.summary: A locust is a type of grasshopper that can form huge swarms and eat crops very quickly.
animals.habitat: Dry grasslands and deserts of Africa and Asia
animals.fun: A big swarm can contain billions of locusts.

animals.name: Tarantula
animals.alt: A hairy tarantula on a white background
animals.summary: Large, hairy spiders found in tropical and subtropical regions. Some live in ground burrows and others live in trees.
animals.habitat: Deserts, rainforests and grasslands, mostly in warm regions
animals.fun: Many tarantulas flick tiny hairs from their abdomen at attackers.

animals.name: Scorpion
animals.alt: A scorpion with its tail raised
animals.summary: Scorpions have a segmented tail that curves over the back and ends in a venomous stinger, plus a pair of pincers.
animals.habitat: Deserts, grasslands and forests on most continents
animals.fun: Under ultraviolet light, a scorpion glows blue-green.

animals.name: Black widow
animals.alt: A black widow spider with a red hourglass marking
animals.summary: Black widows have glossy black bodies, often with a red or orange hourglass on the belly. They are known for their strong venom.
animals.habitat: Sheds, woodpiles and quiet corners in warm regions
animals.diet: Insects caught in a messy web
animals.fun: Only the bite of the larger females is a serious risk to people, and bites are rare.

animals.name: Fat-tailed scorpion
animals.alt: A pale fat-tailed scorpion on a white background
animals.summary: Known for its thick tail. Some species in this group have venom that is medically significant to humans.
animals.habitat: Deserts of North Africa and the Middle East
animals.fun: Its thick tail gives it a lot of stinging muscle for its size.

animals.name: Wolf spider
animals.alt: A brown wolf spider on a white background
animals.summary: Active hunters known for speed and agility. They do not build webs to catch prey, and females carry their young on their backs.
animals.habitat: Grass, leaf litter and gardens around the world
animals.fun: A mother wolf spider carries her egg sac with her, then her spiderlings.

animals.name: Emperor scorpion
animals.alt: A large black emperor scorpion on a white background
animals.summary: One of the largest scorpions, known for its size and dark colour. It is relatively docile and popular in the pet trade.
animals.habitat: Rainforests and savannas of West Africa
animals.fun: Its sting is mild for a scorpion, so it relies mostly on its big pincers.

animals.name: Snail
animals.alt: A snail on a rotting log
animals.summary: Snails have a spiral shell and move slowly on one muscular foot.
animals.habitat: Gardens, forests, ponds and the sea
animals.fun: A snail leaves a trail of slime that helps it glide and protects its foot.

animals.name: Clam
animals.alt: A handful of clams
animals.summary: Clams have two shells hinged together and live buried in sand or mud.
animals.habitat: Seabeds, estuaries and some freshwater
animals.diet: Tiny plankton filtered from the water
animals.fun: Some clams can live for more than 100 years.

animals.name: Squid
animals.alt: A translucent squid swimming in blue water
animals.summary: Squids are fast swimmers with eight arms and two longer tentacles.
animals.habitat: Oceans worldwide, from the surface to the deep sea
animals.fun: The giant squid can reach about 12 metres long, longer than a bus.

animals.name: Octopus
animals.alt: An octopus on a rock underwater
animals.summary: Octopuses are smart animals that can change colour to hide or to signal.
animals.habitat: Coral reefs, rocky shores and the deep sea
animals.fun: An octopus has three hearts and blue blood.

animals.name: Crocodile
animals.alt: A young crocodile held in a person's hand
animals.summary: Crocodiles are powerful reptiles that have changed very little since the age of the dinosaurs.
animals.habitat: Rivers, lakes and wetlands in the tropics
animals.fun: Baby crocodiles call from inside the egg to tell their mother it is time to dig them out.

animals.name: Iguana
animals.alt: A green lizard with a spiny crest
animals.summary: A large lizard with a row of spines along its back. Many iguanas spend their days basking in the sun.
animals.habitat: Tropical forests and rocky coasts of the Americas
animals.fun: Some iguanas can stay underwater for up to 30 minutes.

animals.name: Leopard gecko
animals.alt: A spotted orange and yellow leopard gecko on a rock
animals.summary: A small, spotted lizard that hunts at night. It stores fat in its tail.
animals.habitat: Dry, rocky deserts of Pakistan and Afghanistan
animals.fun: Unlike many geckos, it has eyelids and cannot climb glass.

animals.name: Tuatara
animals.alt: A tuatara beside green fern leaves
animals.summary: A rare reptile found only in New Zealand. It looks like a lizard but belongs to its own ancient group.
animals.habitat: Offshore islands of New Zealand
animals.fun: Tuataras can live for more than 60 years in the wild.

animals.name: Snake
animals.alt: The scaly head of a snake
animals.summary: Snakes are limbless reptiles with no eyelids or ears. They smell the air with their tongues.
animals.habitat: Deserts, forests, oceans and grasslands on every continent except Antarctica
animals.diet: Mice, birds, eggs, fish or insects (all are carnivores)
animals.fun: A snake can swallow animals much wider than its own head.

animals.name: Sea turtle
animals.alt: A sea turtle swimming above a sandy seabed
animals.summary: A reptile that spends its life at sea. Females return to land only to lay eggs on sandy beaches.
animals.habitat: Warm and temperate oceans
animals.diet: Seagrass, jellyfish or crabs, depending on the species
animals.fun: Sea turtles often return to the same beach where they hatched.
